title: fix(lint)!: an FLS key with an empty object part ('.FIELD') is refused as unqualified, at os validate and the save door alike
body:
Fixes #23549

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

A permission set's `fields` key whose object part is empty (`'.full_name'`) was saved, passed both field-permission (FLS) lint rules, and never enforced. `security-fls-unqualified-key` now refuses it, so `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` and the metadata save door answer alike. One file of rule code changes (`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`); no rule id, error code, export, schema or migration entry is added.

## The narrowing, checkable from this body

`PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions` applies a set's field rules to object O only for keys that start with `O.`, and `ObjectSchema.name` is `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/`, so no object is named by the empty string: a key with an empty object part can never match, and the mask it declares never applies, for every holder of the set.

Measured through `validateSecurityPosture` on one stack (object `crm_account` with field `description`, one permission set granting it). Before = `origin/main` `8226755ee`; after = this branch. The save-door column is the real kernel pin below.

| `fields` key | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `'.description'` | no finding; the save door stores it (`success: true`) | `security-fls-unqualified-key` (error); the save door answers `422 INVALID_METADATA` with exactly that one issue |
| `'.'`, `'..description'`, `'.description.x'` | no finding | `security-fls-unqualified-key` (error), one finding per key |
| `'description'` (bare) | `security-fls-unqualified-key`; save door 422 | unchanged, same message and fix line |
| `'crm_account.'`, `'crm_account.description.x'` (in-stack object) | `security-fls-unknown-field`; save door 422 | unchanged |
| `'no_such_object.x'`, `'no_such_object.'` (an object another package may declare) | no finding; saves | unchanged |
| `'crm_account.description'` (a real field) | no finding; saves | unchanged |

The new verdict, as `validateSecurityPosture` prints it for `'.description'`. The runtime text spells the form with angle-bracket placeholders, which this page would strip, so it is written OBJECT.FIELD here:

- message: `field-permission key '.description' is not object-qualified — its object part (before the first '.') is empty, so the key matches no object, is silently IGNORED, and the declared masking never enforces.`
- fix line: `Name the object before the '.': FLS keys take the 'OBJECT.FIELD' form, e.g. 'crm_opportunity.description'.` The example is given only when the remainder is one plain name. For `'.'`, `'..x'` and `'.x.y'` the fix line names the form alone, because `'crm_opportunity.'` or `'crm_opportunity..x'` would be refused in turn by `security-fls-unknown-field`.

**Where it now refuses.** Every door that runs this lint: `os validate`, `os build` (and `os compile`, which `os dev` runs), `os lint`, `os verify`, the scaffold check; and at runtime a `permission` write in publish mode through `saveMetaItem` (REST `/meta`, Studio, MCP) and the promotion of a draft (`publishMetaItem`). Publish-mode saves through `saveMetaItem` on the environment authoring channel inherit it: permission-set clone, `duplicatePackage`, the unmanaged-package import and the organization-ownership ceremony. A kernel assembled on the `package-author` authoring channel skips the gate (`protocol.ts` :6951); the author-time CLI doors judge that channel's source instead. A draft save is never gated.

**What is not narrowed.** Reads, boot and artifact loading: no load path runs this lint (measured, H4 below). An `os migrate meta --stored --apply` re-save (`migrateStoredMetadata`) is not judged either: the gate exempts `source: 'migrate-stored'` (`protocol.ts` :6967, and `saveMetaItem` :22654), so a stored set holding such a key is rewritten into the current dialect unjudged, is not reported `failed`, and keeps loading; its next ordinary publish-mode save is judged. `OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES=1` still turns the refusal into a logged write.

## Which rule owns it (the H2 reading implemented)

An empty object part IS an unqualified key. The id (*unqualified*), the runtime consequence (the key matches nothing) and the remedy (qualify the key with its object) all fit, so a consumer acting on the rule id has no second branch to take, which is the lane charter's test for widening the existing member rather than minting a code. The guard changes from "contains a `.`" to "has a non-empty object part before its first `.`" (`dot > 0` is qualified). The message needed a second shape sentence (a bare-key message says "a bare key", which `'.x'` is not), and the fix line names the form. `security-fls-unknown-field` gains the matching `dot === 0` skip, so the two loops keep disjoint guards and each key earns one finding. Both shapes share the one existing `findings.push` site, so the file's push-site count pin (16) is unchanged. `rule-explanations.ts` is untouched: `security-fls-unqualified-key` has no entry there, and the unknown-field entry names no guard.

## Mechanism measurements (H1, H3, H4, H5)

- **H1, confirmed.** The new pins were committed first (`1e6a4a321`, tests only, on the `8226755ee` source) and run before the fix: the six new unit cases were red (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'security-fls-unqualified-key' ]`, all empty-object-part spellings), and the save-door case was red (`the save of fields key ".full_name" must be refused: expected undefined to be defined`, i.e. the save resolved). Every control passed in the same runs.
- **H3, edges.** The table above. After the change: `'.'`, `'..x'`, `'.x.y'` and `'.FIELD'` go to `security-fls-unqualified-key` only; `'crm_account.'` stays with `security-fls-unknown-field`; no key earns two findings or none.
- **H4, who else runs this lint.** The CLI author-time doors (`runAuthoringRules` for `validate` / `build` / `lint`, `judgeAuthorTimeRules` for `os verify`, `scaffold-validate` for `os init`) judge source config. The runtime gate (`evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate`) runs only from `saveMetaItem` and `promoteDraftForPublish`, both write verbs. No other runtime package calls the lint (`@objectstack/lint` is imported in `src` only by `metadata-protocol` and `cli`), and the gate's D4 contract leaves stored rows reading. Measured on a real kernel (ObjectKernel + ObjectQLPlugin, a temporary test not committed): a set holding `'.full_name'` stored ACTIVE through the operator hatch (the shape a row written before this change has) survives a reboot of a fresh kernel over the same store (no throw), reads back with the key, and is in the registry; its re-save without the hatch answers `422 INVALID_METADATA` `["security-fls-unqualified-key"]`; a draft re-save still lands. No conversion or migration entry is built.
- **H5, corpus.** 0 `fields` keys starting with `.` in `examples/`, `skills/`, `packages/` fixtures, templates and docs at `8226755ee`. The one textual hit, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json:707`, is prose abbreviating `'showcase_project.spent'`, not a key.

## Tests

All through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`. The current head `d72dd9639` adds only a changeset prose repair on top of `8e4f65c2c`; `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:empty-changeset` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` re-ran there, all exit 0. At `8e4f65c2c` (this branch merged with `origin/main` `086fa4640` before opening):

- `@objectstack/lint` `pnpm test`: 139 files, 6755 passed; `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0.
- the save-door pin, `packages/objectql/src/protocol-save-permission-fls-key-forms.test.ts` (`--project local`): 6 passed. It boots ObjectKernel + ObjectQLPlugin over an in-memory driver and asserts `code` + `status` + the issue list, and the stored rows:
  - `'.full_name'` refused `422 INVALID_METADATA`, issues `['security-fls-unqualified-key']`, the fix line naming the form, nothing stored;
  - a draft carrying it saves, and its publish is refused the same way with no active row written;
  - CONTROLS, unchanged: the bare key (422, unqualified-key) and the deeper key `flskey_customer.full_name.x` (422, unknown-field);
  - NEGATIVE CONTROLS: `flskey_customer.full_name` and `no_such_object.x` both save and are stored as written.
- `@objectstack/objectql` `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0 (the new file compiles; no test-typecheck ledger growth).
- Consumer packages (the contract-face run). At `57db599dd`, the pre-merge head (same diff): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` 236 files, 28409 passed, 19 skipped; `@objectstack/plugin-security` 185 files, 3690 passed, 45 skipped; `@objectstack/objectql` `--project local` 420 files, 8119 passed. At `8e4f65c2c`: `@objectstack/cli` `--project unit` `test/data-model-rules.test.ts` + `test/explain-rule-id.test.ts`, 70 passed; `packages/qa/dogfood` `test/showcase-permission-zoo.dogfood.test.ts`, 10 passed. The merge brought nothing into `lint`, `objectql` or `metadata-protocol`, so those three were not re-run in full after it; their targeted pins were.

## Ablation (one, on the widened guard)

Fix committed first (`0b318c1c3`). Mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 → 0, marker 0 → 1, blob `c25d7b17c299` → `0995d0684e9d`): the guard `if (dot > 0) continue;` narrowed back to `dot >= 0` (the old "contains a `.`" skip) with a build-surviving marker; `@objectstack/lint` rebuilt; `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` found the marker in 4 built files. Result: the lint file 6 failed / 160 passed (exactly the six new empty-object-part cases), the save-door pin 1 failed / 4 passed (the `'.full_name'` case: "expected undefined to be defined"). Restore: `git checkout HEAD`, blob == HEAD (`c25d7b17c299`), `git diff HEAD` empty; rebuilt; preflight `--absent` (marker absent from all 20 built files, tree clean); the lint file 166 passed, the pin 5 passed. Direction observed: turns red, as expected.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 65 families from the merge base (identical to the dispatch's lead derivation at `8226755ee`). At `8e4f65c2c` all 65 ran locally and exited 0, each exit captured before any pipe; `dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` reconciles 65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun. Among them, on this diff: `check:adr-0087-registration` (one declared-breaking changeset, disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), `check:empty-changeset`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:objectql-double-limit`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:nul-bytes`. The required contexts and the full battery are this PR's check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- `security-fls-unqualified-key` has no `os explain` entry in `rule-explanations.ts`. This PR adds none, because #22161's census slices own that file. Noted, not filed.
- The changeset states the before and the now for `'.FIELD'` in words, not under a literal FROM → TO label. `check:adr-0087-registration` reads a label-positioned FROM/TO placeholder as a migration prescription, which contradicts the `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition that fits here: `os migrate meta` cannot derive which object an empty object part meant, so no ledger entry can carry the repair, and the dispatch rules out a migration entry. The gate is green on the changeset as written.
- The changeset is `minor` for `@objectstack/lint`, the launch-window convention the other accept-set narrowings in this train use. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` gets no bump: its code does not change, it runs the lint it depends on.
